payload.goal: Find an overdue customer invoice, add a dunning fee of 60 NOK via ledger posting (debit receivables 1500, credit dunning fees 3400), create and send an invoice for the fee to the same customer, and register a partial payment of 5000 NOK on the overdue invoice.
likely_resources: invoice list/search endpoint with due date and status filters
product endpoint for dunning fee item
success_checks: An overdue customer invoice is identified with unpaid balance remaining before payment
A voucher is posted with debit account 1500 = 60 NOK and credit account 3400 = 60 NOK
A fee invoice for 60 NOK is created for the same customer
The fee invoice is sent successfully
A payment of 5000 NOK is registered against the overdue invoice
The overdue invoice balance is reduced by exactly 5000 NOK after payment
risk_notes: Sandbox is empty, so no actual overdue invoice/customer may exist; may require creating bootstrap customer/order/invoice first if none found
Prompt does not specify which customer/invoice; selection criteria for 'the overdue invoice' are ambiguous if multiple exist
VAT on dunning fee is not stated; dunning fees are often VAT-exempt, but this can vary by setup
Payment method, payment date, and bank account are not provided
Creating a separate fee invoice in addition to ledger posting may duplicate fee recognition depending on accounting policy
Sending invoice requires valid customer contact details/email or delivery method
payload.suggested_first_action: Search invoices for overdue unpaid customer invoices and select the target invoice/customer.

If no customer/invoice exists in empty sandbox: create bank account/module prerequisites, then POST /customer, POST /order, POST /order/{id}/orderline, POST /order/{id}/invoice to bootstrap an overdue invoice scenario
Select target overdue invoice and read its customerId and outstanding amount
POST /ledger/voucher with lines: debit account 1500 amount 60 NOK, credit account 3400 amount 60 NOK, reference to customer/invoice if supported
Ensure a product exists for dunning fee; if not, POST /product with description 'Mahngebühr', price 60, VAT as configured
POST /order/{id}/orderline with dunning fee item quantity 1 price 60
POST /order/{id}/invoice to create invoice for the dunning fee
POST /invoice/{overdueInvoiceId}/payment with amount 5000 NOK as partial payment
Verify updated balances on both the overdue invoice and the fee invoice

planned_endpoints.summary: Find invoices corresponding with sent data. Includes charged outgoing invoices only.
Add new voucher. IMPORTANT: Also creates postings. Only the gross amounts will be used. Amounts should be rounded to 2 decimals.

rules: ALWAYS set BOTH amountGross AND amountGrossCurrency to the SAME value on every posting.
Do NOT include postings with row=0 — row 0 is system-generated and will cause a 422.
AUTO-SPLIT RULES: ONLY vatType id=3 (25% utgående) triggers auto-split. vatType id=1 does NOT auto-split.
For supplier costs: use vatType=3 (NOT id=1) with ONLY the debit posting. Tripletex detects the expense account and applies inngående MVA automatically.
For vatType=0: include BOTH debit AND credit postings manually. They must sum to 0.
If you get 422 'postings don't sum to 0': switch to vatType=3 with single debit posting, OR add both debit+credit with vatType=0.
NEVER use vatType=1 — it does NOT auto-generate balancing entries and will always cause 422 with single posting.
Do NOT include currency on postings — let it default. Including currency={} causes 'factor must be >= 1' error.
For supplier invoices, set supplier={"id": supplier_id} on the debit posting.
Resolve account numbers: GET /ledger/account with params={"number": XXXX}, then use account={"id": resolved_id}. NEVER use account={"number": XXXX} in postings.
ALWAYS search first if product_number is provided: GET /product?number=<number> — sandbox pre-seeds products.
Only POST /product if GET returns 0 results.
Use 'number' field for the product number (NOT productNumber).
priceExcludingVat sets the base price. Also set vatType={"id": 3|5|6}.
Set orderDate and deliveryDate (use today_iso from execution_brief).

what_went_wrong: GET /invoice called without required invoiceDateFrom/invoiceDateTo params, causing 422 validation error — these params are documented as required.
First POST /ledger/voucher omitted the customer field on the receivables posting (account 1500), causing a 422 'Kunde mangler' error before retrying successfully.
what_worked: All 3 scoring checks passed (7/7 raw score, normalized 1.33) — full correctness achieved.
Enforcer override was used correctly to distinguish bootstrap invoice from dunning fee invoice, and all key steps (voucher, invoice, send, payment) completed successfully.
what_to_try_next: Skip GET /invoice entirely since the sandbox is known to be empty at start — saves 1 call and eliminates the 422 error.
Include customer field on the debit posting (account 1500) in the first voucher attempt to avoid the retry — know upfront that receivables postings require a customer reference.
Combine the bank account PUT and order POST into a single parallel batch to reduce sequential latency, and pre-include invoiceDateFrom/invoiceDateTo if ever querying invoices.
unnecessary_calls: GET /invoice — sandbox is empty, this call always fails without required date params and provides no useful info.
GET /ledger/account — account IDs were already pre-resolved in the agent's context, making this lookup redundant.
